OOD_Wikipedia_2023.claim: TEMPORAL. Same source family as the Pile's Wikipedia component, but a 2023-11 snapshot. Revisions written after the ~2020 Pile snapshot cannot have been in it. Confounds: three years of new entities, events and editorial convention move with the exclusion. This is external review's PRIMARY recommended panel because it holds language and register nearly fixed.
OOD_Wikipedia_2023.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

OOD_arXiv_2023.claim: TEMPORAL. 2023 arXiv papers; the Pile's arXiv component predates the snapshot. Stable LaTeX/scientific register. Confounds: new terminology, fields, authors; heavy template reuse means short-k overlap will be high regardless of exposure.
OOD_arXiv_2023.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

OOD_News_2024.claim: TEMPORAL. June 2024 news, four years past the snapshot. Ordinary English, so it tests transport without immediately confounding on script or competence. Confounds: news register, named entities, and possible syndication into web crawls.
OOD_News_2024.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

OOD_CommonPile.claim: PROVENANCE. Assembled later from openly-licensed and public-domain sources, covering domains not deliberately represented in the Pile. Tests whether the effect is about corpus construction/licensing rather than topic. Confounds: licence filtering changes the source population; some documents may still be older web material.
OOD_CommonPile.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

TRAP_FineWeb.claim: DELIBERATE POSITIVE CONTROL, NOT A CLEAN Q. FineWeb is Common-Crawl-derived and Pile-CC is too, so it can contain the same pages, later versions of them, or mirrors. Both external review reviews name CC derivatives as a trap. Included so M1 has something it MUST flag as overlapping: if FineWeb does not show high containment, M1 is broken.
TRAP_FineWeb.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

CONTROL_PubMed_2023.claim: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN. The Pile contains PubMed Central, so this is source-INCLUDED; only post-snapshot articles would be temporally excluded and this dump is not date-filtered. Expected to land BETWEEN the Pile components and the temporal panels, which makes it a useful mid-scale reference point for whatever divergence metric we fit.
CONTROL_PubMed_2023.status: CANDIDATE — outside-Pile is a HYPOTHESIS to be measured by M1, not a property asserted here

OOD_News_2024_dedup.seed_blocks_note: computed as b = len(texts) // 3 at load time (experiments/trainval.py:256), so the blocks are NOT the 800/1600/2400 of the n=2400 corpora. Recorded explicitly because this corpus is shorter than every other entry here.
OOD_News_2024_dedup.hf_note: INTENTIONALLY null. This corpus has NO independent upstream. It is produced deterministically from OOD_News_2024 by the rule below and must never be given a fabricated dataset revision. To regenerate it, rebuild the parent at the revision pinned in corpora/dataset_revisions.json and re-apply the rule.

derived_from.rule: exact-text deduplication: keep the FIRST occurrence of each distinct `text` value, preserving the parent's record order; drop every later exact duplicate
derived_from.rule_verified: verified 2026-09-01 by recomputation: first-occurrence dedup of the parent reproduces this file's text sequence exactly (order-sensitive equality True); sorted(distinct) does NOT (False), so the order is first-occurrence, not sorted

OOD_News_2024_dedup.claim: DERIVED CONTROL. The 2024-06 BBC News panel with its 802 exact-duplicate records removed. It exists because the parent contains syndicated/repeated articles, which inflate any recurrence-based statistic. It is NOT an independent OOD rung: it shares the parent's upstream, register and time window entirely.
OOD_News_2024_dedup.status: DERIVED — provenance is the parent's plus the recorded rule. Excluded BY DESIGN from the E48b containment index (experiments/t48b_exposure_growth.py:77-81 --exclude default): it was created after the k-gram shards were built and is a strict subset of OOD_News_2024, so indexing it would double-count the parent's k-grams.
OOD_News_2024_dedup.recorded_why: this corpus had operators fitted on it but NO entry in this manifest and NO row in corpora/dataset_revisions.json, whose README claims to be the source of truth for every corpus build. Gap closed by recording the derivation, not by inventing an upstream pin.
